myth.title: Lymphatic drainage detoxes you and melts fat
myth.claim: Lymphatic drainage pulls toxins out of the body and causes fat or weight loss.
myth.harm_reason: Sources say there is no evidence it causes weight loss and the toxin claims are unfounded. The massage itself is not described as harmful.
myth.match_note: Topic: exact phrase "lymphatic drainage" in transcript, caption or on-screen text. Claim: a separate fuzzy search for "lymphatic detox", "lymphatic toxins", "lymphatic debloat", "lymphatic weight loss" or "lymphatic flush" in transcript or caption.

quoted.quote: It's the easiest way to get inflammation out of the body, detox, and wake up.

verdict: There's no good evidence that lymphatic drainage detoxes you or causes weight loss. It can reduce swelling for a while, and it plays a real role in treating lymphedema.
what_is_true: It can reduce swelling and give a temporary slimmer, tighter look (UCLA Health).
It plays a critical role in treating lymphedema (UCLA Health).
what_is_false: That it causes weight loss. There is no evidence for that (UCLA Health, National Geographic).
That it gets rid of toxins. Those claims are unfounded (National Geographic).
